overall_reason: The idea is 'most tools manage projects or people; Consile does both in one workspace', and the hero shows it with a product dashboard, but from 'See Consile in two minutes' onward the page becomes a stock run of pill eyebrows and identical icon-card grids that would hold under any team-ops SaaS.

score.reason: T-ONE-SENTENCE and T-KIND-FIT pass on the hero, but T-SIGNATURE finds a greeting over four stat cards, T-IDEA-CARRIES fails from the second section, T-DEFAULT-PLAN marks five moves and most headings survive T-RIVAL-NAME.

findings.title: One idea runs the whole artifact
findings.where: from 'See Consile in two minutes' to the footer, 1440px (tiles/1440-01.png to 1440-07.png)
findings.evidence: T-IDEA-CARRIES fails at the second section. After the hero, the page shows no more product UI: the demo video poster is a grey panel with five initial tiles ('PR', 'TB', 'TT', 'HR', 'LV'), then 'Why teams struggle without Consile', 'How Consile solves it', a grid of about twenty identical icon cards ('Running in Minutes, Not Months', 'SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On', 'Cookie Consent'), a stat strip, 'Choose your way in', six security cards and a FAQ. None of them shows tasks and people data joined, which is the idea.
findings.before: Text-only icon cards for every module and promise
findings.after: Show the join the hero promises: one screen where a leave approval changes the task board, or a KPI review pulls attendance, then cut the module grid to the few that prove it
findings.why: The one specific claim on the page, projects and people in one place, is shown once and then replaced by a feature inventory any HR or task tool could publish.

findings.title: One real signature on the first screen
findings.evidence: T-SIGNATURE finds a stand-in (draft CON-119). The dashboard opens 'Good morning, Otto' over four stat cards ('TASKS DUE 18', 'ATTENDANCE 92%', 'PEOPLE 35', 'REVIEWS 6') and a donut '92% present', in a workspace named 'Acme Studio' and labelled 'PRODUCT PREVIEW · SAMPLE DATA'. The frame shows totals, not the product's distinct object.
findings.before: Greeting over four stat cards and a donut
findings.after: Lead with the screen only Consile has: for example a task list where each assignee shows today's attendance or leave status beside the work
findings.why: A greeting over stat cards is the default dashboard picture, so the one product image does not show what makes this product different.

findings.title: Refuse the default plan
findings.evidence: T-DEFAULT-PLAN marks five moves: three numbered problem cards ('1 Tool Overload', '2 Flying Blind', '3 Manual Busywork'); small pill eyebrows on every section ('The problem', 'The solution', 'Features', 'FAQ'); a label-and-value strip between hairlines ('27 BUILT-IN MODULES', '99.9% MONTHLY UPTIME TARGET', 'Free STARTER PLAN UP TO 5 USERS'); a closing band 'Ready to run tasks, people ops, and performance from one workspace?'; a dark footer with long link columns. The page also uses a pale ground with one orange accent.
findings.before: Problem, solution, features, security, journeys, beliefs, security again, FAQ, CTA
findings.after: Merge the two security sections, drop the problem-solution pair, and order what remains by the buyer's question
findings.why: The stock order and repeated card grids make the page read as filled from a template despite the specific hero.

findings.title: Every large decision belongs to this client
findings.evidence: T-RIVAL-NAME: with Connecteam or Factorial in place of Consile, 'One Platform, Zero Chaos', 'Real-Time Team Pulse', 'Workflows That Run Themselves', 'Enterprise-grade by default', 'Built with security & compliance at the core', 'Speed is a feature' and 'Questions, answered' all stay true. The hero motto '"Connecting Teams. Empowering Work."' also holds under any rival.
findings.before: 'One Platform, Zero Chaos' / '"Connecting Teams. Empowering Work."'
findings.after: Keep the lines that only Consile can say ('Most tools only manage projects or only manage people') and rewrite the rest from product facts
findings.why: Most headings would sit unchanged on a competitor's page, so they spend the visitor's attention without separating the product.

findings.title: Every headline promise is pictured
findings.evidence: T-PROMISE-PICTURED fails. 'Shifts, Rotations & Swap Requests', 'Guided Onboarding for New Hires' and 'KPI Reviews & Performance Tracking' each make a concrete promise and are pictured only by a small orange line icon.
findings.after: One product screenshot for each of the three modules that carry the idea (shifts, leave, reviews)
findings.why: A buyer comparing HR tools needs to see the shift swap or the review screen, and the page shows an icon instead.

strengths: T-ONE-SENTENCE passes on the hero: 'Most tools only manage projects or only manage people. Consile brings both together' is a positioning only this product claims, and the audience line 'Built for growing teams of 2–200' is specific.
T-KIND-FIT passes on the first screen: software leads with its own UI (sidebar with Tasks, Attendance, People, Performance), and the frame is honestly labelled 'SAMPLE DATA'.
The security cards are concrete ('HMAC-signed outgoing webhooks', 'Six built-in role tiers', 'AES-256 at rest') and should stay as material, merged into one section.
not_investigated: 00-contract.md is absent; visitor mode read as Persuade from the page itself.
The demo video was not played; only its poster frame was judged.
At 375 an 'Install Consile' prompt covers the lower hero (tiles/375-00.png); it is the site's own overlay, judged for concept only as context.
